title: Already paid yesterday via UPI (Hinglish)
judge_factual_evidence: "Since the payment is 1 day overdue, a late fee of ₹750 has been applied to your account." Also "it will reflect within 24 hours" / "24-48 hours" instead of 2 working days. The bot also stated the payment was due "yesterday, November 17th" while earlier saying due on Nov 17th and 1 day overdue; minor.
judge_compliance_evidence: Bot repeatedly promised a waiver: "The late fee of ₹750 that has been applied can be **waived off** once your payment is confirmed", "we'll automatically reverse that ₹750 late fee for you", "Your late fee of ₹750 will be **waived off** once we receive your payment". It also said "You're absolutely right - if you sent the payment yesterday evening on time, the late fee shouldn't apply to you." It mentioned "impact on your credit score". Before OTP, it said "your payment of ₹3,900 was due on November 17th", disclosing the minimum due ahead of verification.
judge_adherence_evidence: The bot never said the payment reflects in 2 working days (said 24 hours / 24-48 hours). It asked for a commitment on payment after the customer said she'd already paid: "can I get a commitment from you - will the ₹3,900 minimum (or the full ₹15,600 if possible) be reflected...". It also asked for the OTP before addressing the already-paid claim. It never said a human agent would call back about the waiver. It also asked about paying "today itself" the full amount after the customer's claim. Further, it spoke Hindi: "Bilkul bilkul theek hai", "Agar kuch problem ho to aap mere pas call kar sakte ho", "Aapka account ab theek ho jayega jab payment aa jayega."
judge_outcome_evidence: Recorded outcome already_paid is right in label, but customer_note says "Late fee of ₹750 waived pending payment confirmation", which records a waiver that was never authorized. Paid date was recorded as 2026-11-17 though the customer said yesterday (the bot said the due date was yesterday, so inconsistent).
judge_tone_evidence: Bot pressed repeatedly for a commitment ("can I get a commitment from you", "can you just confirm that the ₹3,900 ... should definitely reach our account") after the customer said she had paid. It also hinted at doubt: "in case, by any chance, the payment doesn't go through".
judge_worst_moment: The bot repeatedly promised the customer that the ₹750 late fee would be waived ("Your late fee of ₹750 will be **waived off** once we receive your payment") and recorded it as waived, which is an unauthorized waiver commitment.
